plugins.name: secret-input-card
plugins.description: Use any API key, token or password without exposing it in the chat: you paste it into a protected card, the plugin saves it to a gitignored .env file or the macOS Keychain, and Claude gets only the variable name, so the programs it runs can use the secret.

plugins.name: staging-vostro
plugins.description: Puts a Novantir app on the home lab server as a client prototype or permanent staging, following the lab manual: deploy/lab compose contract, one-time project setup, Cognito, manual and automatic deploy, Cloudflare Tunnel hostnames and Linear tracking.

plugins.name: full-stop-send
plugins.description: Takes an issue to a merge-ready pull request with proof, an independent review and green CI, then stops (Full Stop). Merges on its own (Full Send) only for the change class a repository allows in writing, with the full gate. Closes the issue at the end with a case study, follow-up issues and troubleshooting notes.

plugins.name: novo-projeto
plugins.description: Starts a new Novantir project the way the existing ones are laid out: folder under the right category of ~/projects (produtos, jogos, tools, oficina), git, an AGENTS.md from the category template, README, .gitignore and, for products, the docs/ skeleton with the process settings; GitHub repo and cockpit registration prepared for the owner's OK.

plugins.name: revisao-pr
plugins.description: Reviews a pull request the way the Claude Code team does: parallel reviewers that see only the diff, independent verifiers that vote on each finding before it is posted, findings tagged Important / Nit / Pre-existing with file:line evidence, review depth set by the risk of the change, diff-only re-review with a round cap, and a record of what happened to each finding.

plugins.name: ronda
plugins.description: Periodic upkeep of a repository in five modes, each with its own short report: production health, security sweep, dependencies and AI models, docs coherence, and a small code cleanup. Reads the repository's own settings from docs/processo/ronda.md and never touches git; a scheduled run posts its report as a single comment on the repository's routine issue.
